reviewer: primary Codex direct inspection of formal original-resolution stills and complete 24-frame clip

answers.reason: The orange pebbled, three-seam actor reads as a basketball; each target has a bottle body, shoulder, neck, cap and label.
The 0.24 m diameter basketball and 0.28 m bottles have plausible real-world proportions.
The formal setup and clip show distinct blue low, orange medium and green high liquid surfaces separate from the label bands.
The complete clip shows continuous ball contact, direct high-mass response and propagation into both rear branches; no simultaneous pose jump appears.
Measured native blur adds speed while preserving basketball seams, bottle silhouettes, caps, labels and the left-to-right contact direction.
The aftermath contains solver-discovered radial separation, support contacts and different bottle rotations rather than a neat placed arrangement.
Native glass refraction, exact internal liquid levels, highlights, ball pebbling and contact shadows are more credible than PC8 abstract wooden targets.

qualitativeLimitations: EEVEE glass refraction still shows real-time rendering artifacts and is not advertising-grade photoreal glass
liquid is a static fill-derived column and does not simulate slosh
bottles and ball do not deform and no sound was evaluated
claimCeiling: PASS establishes a product-integrated metric basketball/filled-bottle rigid-body lesson with visible-state-derived mass and COM, native measured blur, solver-owned post-release motion and exact reopen. It does not establish liquid dynamics, deformation, photorealism, broad asset generalization or robot-capstone quality.
